title: Servicing System Reference — Default-Rate Interest Entries on Farm Real Estate Loans
content:
**Product:** Farm Real Estate Loans · **Subject:** the default-rate interest entry on an installment paid in full after its trigger

## The rule

Default-rate interest is owed on an installment that was paid in full more than the trigger days after it fell due, and the entry for it is booked as soon as the desk finds it missing; the installment considered is the most recent installment bill, together with the most recent scheduled principal payment, which is the payment that completed it.

The default-rate interest entry carries only the default-interest add-on, because the contract-rate interest for the same days is billed with the regular installment, and it is booked as its own interest entry marked as default-rate interest, dated the day it is booked.

## Business effect

| Before | After the entry is booked |
|---|---|
| The installment was paid in full late and the loan's history shows no default-rate interest entry for it | The loan's transaction history shows a new interest entry marked as default-rate interest, with its period, rate and amount, dated the day it is booked |
| Billed interest owed stands at its earlier figure | Billed interest owed rises by the amount of the entry |

## Tool: `book_default_interest_ef623284`

**What it does.** It books a default-rate interest entry on a farm real estate loan and adds it to the billed interest owed: one interest entry at the default rate covering the stretch of days given, dated and billed today; the loan's billed-interest-not-yet-paid balance rises by the amount. The entry is booked exactly as given.

**How it is invoked.** It is a servicing-desk tool, owned by the agent: the desk unlocks `book_default_interest_ef623284` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `loan_id` | the loan number of the member's farm real estate loan, read from the farm real estate loan lookup | the loan number as shown on the loan record |
| `period_start` | the first day the default-rate entry covers, inclusive | YYYY-MM-DD; never empty here |
| `period_end` | the last day the default-rate entry covers, inclusive | YYYY-MM-DD; never empty here |
| `rate_applied` | the annual rate the entry is figured at | annual percentage rate, in percent, 3 decimal places; never empty here |
| `amount` | the interest booked | USD, 2 decimal places, always positive; rounded half-up to cents as received |

**Return.** A confirmation sentence naming the new entry reference (an id beginning `dfi_`), the loan number, the period covered, the rate and the amount booked, and the loan's new billed interest owed in USD with 2 decimal places. The presence of the entry reference means the entry was recorded. No other return or error is defined for this tool.

## Questions this page answers

**Which installment does the rule look at?** The most recent installment bill on the loan, together with the most recent scheduled principal payment, which is the payment that completed it.

**When is the entry booked?** As soon as the desk finds it missing.

**Does the entry repeat the contract-rate interest?** No. It carries only the default-interest add-on; the contract-rate interest for the same days is billed with the regular installment.

**What date does the entry carry?** The day it is booked.
